name: Stamps BioDesign Studio
org: University of Michigan Stamps School of Art and Design
what_you_do: Work with a U-M engineering research group on medical implant surfaces. Make 2D and 3D patterns, take electron microscope images, then turn them into art.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 10 to 11. A small group is chosen.
pay_detail: Free (grant funded). Daily lunch, local field trips and materials are included.
duration: 4 weeks, Monday to Thursday, 9 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. (July 13 to August 6 in 2026). Commuter program: you do not stay overnight.
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are closed. The early action deadline was February 1, 2026 and the final deadline was March 1, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: Send 5 images of your work, a 250 word personal statement and an unofficial transcript when applications open on the Stamps summer page.
notes: The 2026 program was new and based on Dr. Jouha Min's lab in the College of Engineering. Student artwork can go to the BioArtography program.
